content: A vapor-liquid separator is a vertically oriented vessel designed to separate a mixture of liquid and vapor. When the mixture is introduced into the separator, the liquid component is separated by the force of gravity, causing it to collect at the bottom of the vessel, from where it is subsequently removed. The vapor, on the other hand, rises upward through the vessel at a specific design velocity. This velocity is carefully controlled to minimize the entrainment of liquid droplets within the vapor as it exits the top of the separator. In some cases, the feed entering the vapor-liquid separator may consist of a liquid that undergoes partial or complete flashing into both vapor and liquid phases upon entry into the separator. This process allows for the effective separation of the two phases. A vapor-liquid separator is also known by several alternative names, including a flash drum, knock-out drum, knock-out pot, compressor suction drum, or compressor inlet drum. When the device is specifically used to remove suspended water droplets from air streams, it is commonly referred to as a demister.
